/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/CUSTOM-AGENTS.md:8:*Building* a custom agent means configuring the harness around a stock model: system prompts, a curated toolset, MCP connectors, hooks, restricted-permission subagents, skills. No weights change. This is fully supported, and your marathon/relay stack *is* exactly this — `marathon-agent.sh` routing to per-model shims with containment is a hand-rolled custom agent.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/CUSTOM-AGENTS.md:26:3. **Consider the Claude Agent SDK** if you want hooks, session resume, and file checkpointing for free instead of hand-rolling them — it's the exact agent loop that powers Claude Code, driven from your own Python or TypeScript program. Weigh this against your existing bash containment, which already gives you tighter, more auditable control than the defaults. Don't migrate just to migrate. (Also note the rule of thumb: use an agent only for open-ended problems; if you can hardcode the workflow, a linear script is faster and cheaper — your relay loop is already mostly deterministic, which is correct.)
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/CUSTOM-AGENTS.md:31:Bottom line: don't train. Invest in tools, context, and subagent decomposition on top of the strongest stock model — which is what your marathon stack already does.

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/FEEDBACK/FEEDBACK-KWFS-02.md:7:The cross-repo env contract is undocumented and non-obvious. /Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:37:None of the three harnesses (relay, swarm, marathon) currently emit a durable "this session finished, here's how it went" record. `utils/telemetry/extract-relay-telemetry.sh` (GH-24, closed 2026-06-30) is the closest prior art but is explicitly on-demand/batch — an operator runs it manually against a date range of `relay-system/*.md` files and gets a list. There is no live, automatic append at the moment a session actually completes, and no artifact that all three harness types write to.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:43:- **Relay** → `relay-automation/relay-drive.sh:208-209` — the single point that has verified STATUS is terminal (`Approved`/`Closed`) **and** the tick token is no longer live (agreement check), immediately before `exit 0`. (Not `relay-turn-lib.sh`'s auto tick-done or `poll.sh`'s STATUS read — both check STATUS alone, more loosely, and would double-fire relative to the driver.) **Also hook the non-green exits** — `relay-drive.sh:214-217` (Escalated handback, `health:"orange"`) and the round-cap fallback at `relay-drive.sh:324-330` (`health:"red"` if the post-cap check fails, `"green"` if it happens to pass) — so a stalled or escalated standalone relay isn't silently absent from `XYZ.json` (agy r1 Should).
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:44:- **Marathon** → `relay-automation/marathon.sh:95` — `"$TICK_BIN" log marathon.complete "MARATHON-RUN" --agent marathon`, emitted only after every phase in the plan was approved. This is the whole-run completion; per-phase completions (`marathon-drive.sh:344-346`) are internal and do not each get their own XYZ.json record for a `marathon.sh`-orchestrated run.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:45:- **Swarm** → `swarm-preflight.sh` never executes anything itself — it only produces a packet and writes the operator-facing run command to `run-candidate.json`'s companion `marathon-invocation.txt` (`swarm-preflight.sh:541-547,589`), which invokes `marathon-drive.sh` **directly**, not through `marathon.sh`. This means a swarm-originated run's completion point is `marathon-drive.sh`'s own per-phase completion (`marathon-drive.sh:344-347`), not `marathon.sh:95` — the two are genuinely different code paths, not "the same path distinguished by origin" as an earlier draft of this doc claimed (agy r1 Blocker, corrected).
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:47:**Consequence: `marathon-drive.sh` needs its own completion hook**, independent of `marathon.sh`'s. `marathon.sh` already calls `marathon-drive.sh` per phase, so `marathon-drive.sh`'s hook must stay silent when `XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=marathon-phase` (set by `marathon.sh` around each phase call) and fire when `XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=swarm` (set by `swarm-preflight.sh`'s generated invocation) or when invoked directly with neither flag set (bare single-phase `marathon-drive.sh`, its own `harness:"marathon"` case). Three call shapes, one hook, gated by context:

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:57:`XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT` gates emission at both levels a marathon run nests through, so a `marathon.sh`-orchestrated N-phase run always produces exactly one record, never N or N+1:
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:58:1. **relay-drive.sh level:** `marathon-drive.sh` internally drives a relay loop per phase, so `relay-drive.sh:208-209` fires once per phase *inside* a marathon run. `marathon-drive.sh` sets `XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=marathon-phase` before invoking that relay loop; the relay-drive.sh hook only appends to `XYZ.json` when the flag is unset/`relay` (a standalone `/relay` session), so nested per-phase relay completions never emit their own record.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:59:2. **marathon-drive.sh level:** per the table above, `marathon-drive.sh`'s own hook (`:344-347`) reads the *same* `XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT` to decide whether to emit at all — silent when `marathon.sh` set it to `marathon-phase` (that whole-run summary comes from `marathon.sh:95` instead), firing when it's `swarm` or unset (a swarm-originated or bare `marathon-drive.sh` run, where `marathon-drive.sh`'s own completion *is* the whole run).

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/GH-75-XYZ-JSON-COMPLETION-TELEMETRY.md:63:Per operator decision: swarm-originated runs get `harness: "swarm"`, not folded into `"marathon"`. Concretely, `swarm-preflight.sh` prefixes the `INVOCATION` string it builds (`swarm-preflight.sh:541-547`) with `XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=swarm `, so the exact line it writes to `marathon-invocation.txt` (`swarm-preflight.sh:589`) is self-contained — the operator runs it verbatim and the tag propagates with no extra step (agy r1 Should: this must be explicit in the generated command, not left as a "the operator sets it" assumption).

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:56:This plan is built to run on the **XYZ harness** (`tick` kernel + `relay-automation/` stack), which lives in the `xyz-3-agents-swarm` repo. Two distinct rails do two different jobs — do **not** conflate them:
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:58:- **`tick` / `xyz` swarm = concurrent, path-scoped lanes.** Multiple agents edit **non-overlapping path globs** of ONE shared checkout, in ONE session, claiming lanes with `tick take` / `tick scope --paths <globs>`, heartbeating with `tick ping`, releasing with `tick done`. This is the only rail that gives us *concurrency* (Phase-1 A/B/C and Phase-2 D/E in parallel).
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:59:- **`marathon` = serial, phase-gated relay.** `relay-automation/marathon.sh --plan MARATHON.yaml` runs each phase through one producer↔reviewer relay loop in `depends_on` order, advancing on approval and **halting on the first phase failure**. Marathon does **not** run lanes in parallel — it is the gate that chains phases and enforces review.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:61:**Preflight is a planner, not a launcher.** `utils/swarm-preflight.sh` reads a capture doc's machine-readable preflight contract (see below), proves the fix is still required, assigns lanes, and *emits a run packet*. The **operator** then launches `relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh` with that packet — preflight never executes the run (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES §8).
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:63:**The one rule that makes concurrency work:** No lane starts until Phase 0 freezes `CONTRACTS.md`. Every lane builds against the frozen DB schema, module interfaces, and env-var contract — never against another lane's live code. Cross-lane calls go through interfaces that can be mocked, so a lane is never blocked waiting on a sibling. (`CONTRACTS.md` is the **human** source of truth; the machine surface the harness actually reads is the JSON preflight contract + each lane's `tick --paths` globs.)
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:65:**Cross-repo note.** This plan targets a *separate* greenfield repo (`campaign-data-platform`); the XYZ harness (`swarm-preflight`, `marathon`, `tick`, `validate.sh`, `utils/pdda/pdda.sh`) lives in `xyz-3-agents-swarm`. Phase 0 must therefore **install the harness into the target repo** (via its `install.sh`) so `validate.sh` and `utils/pdda/pdda.sh run` exist locally — or every run must be driven cross-repo with `swarm-preflight --target-root <target>`. Pick one; Phase 0 below assumes the install path.

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:85:**Merge discipline:** Trunk-based. Each lane declares its editable `artifacts` in the preflight contract; a **path-allowlist containment** boundary rejects edits outside a lane's scope. After a lane's turn, marathon-drive runs the contract's `gate` (`bash validate.sh`); `fix_probes` are what proved the work was still required going in. Changes to `CONTRACTS.md` require a dedicated synchronous PR and ping to affected lanes — contracts change by agreement, never silently.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/PROJECT/1-INBOX/TALK-DATA-BUILD.md:87:**Intra-lane order matters, inter-lane order does not.** Tasks in the same lane run in listed order; disjoint lanes have no ordering between them within a phase (that is exactly what lets the swarm run them at once).

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/partc-loop-review.md:55:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/improve-loop.sh:54-56,87-95` does not actually enforce the required positive `--max-iterations`. `improve-loop.sh` only checks that `MAXIT` is non-empty, then ignores `loop-stop.sh`'s exit status; if `--max-iterations` is `0` or `abc`, `loop-stop.sh` exits 2, `dec` is empty, and the `while :` loop keeps running instead of halting. Concrete fix: validate `--max-iterations` in `improve-loop.sh` before the loop and/or treat any non-zero `loop-stop.sh` exit as fatal; add a regression test that invalid `--max-iterations` is rejected by `improve-loop.sh`.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/partc-loop-review.md:56:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/oracle-guard.sh:34-45` relies on `src/paths.js:11-20` string-prefix overlap without canonicalizing paths, so the guard can be bypassed with aliases. Example observed: `bash relay-automation/oracle-guard.sh --allow 'relay-automation/../src/paths.js' --oracle 'src/paths.js'` returns `OK` even though both resolve to the same file; symlink aliases have the same hole. Concrete fix: normalize each allow/oracle entry against the repo root (`path.resolve` + `fs.realpathSync.native` where possible), reject unresolved/escaping paths, then run overlap checks on the canonical forms; add `..` and symlink-path tests.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/partc-loop-review.md:57:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/improve-loop.sh:100` drops `loop-cost.sh`'s `exact|floor` honesty signal with `2>/dev/null`, then feeds only the numeric scalar into spend tracking. In the advertised `--currency tokens --agent agy` path, `loop-cost.sh` emits `0 floor`, but the loop records plain `0`, so `--max-total-budget` can silently never fire even though spend is only a lower bound. Concrete fix: capture and persist the honesty flag in provenance/log output, and fail closed for budget enforcement when spend is a floor (or reject `--currency tokens` for cost-blind agents).
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/partc-loop-review.md:67:- [Blocker 2] oracle-path aliasing bypass — **Implemented.** `oracle-guard.sh` now canonicalizes every allow/oracle entry — `path.resolve` (collapses `..`, absolutizes) + `fs.realpathSync` (resolves symlinks when the path exists) — before the `patternsOverlap` check. Your exact repro (`--allow 'relay-automation/../src/paths.js' --oracle 'src/paths.js'`) now returns OVERLAP (exit 9); a symlink-to-oracle is caught too. Regression: 2 new cases in `test/oracle-guard.sh`.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/partc-loop-review.md:73:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/oracle-guard.sh:43-49` canonicalizes the whole allow/oracle pattern with `path.resolve`, which strips `/**` glob semantics before `src/paths.js` sees it. That re-opens the ancestor-directory hole the guard is supposed to fail closed on: `bash test/oracle-guard.sh` now fails both `src/**` vs `src/paths.js` and `test/**` vs `test/path-overlap.sh`, and `bash test/improve-loop-qa.sh` shows the loop pre-flight returning `0` instead of exit `4` for `--allow "src/**" --oracle-paths "src/paths.js"`. Concrete fix: canonicalize only the literal path portion (or canonicalize the longest literal ancestor, then re-append the wildcard suffix) so wildcard allowlists stay wildcard patterns after normalization, while literal `..` and symlink aliases still collapse to the real path.

/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:60:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/proposals-sink.sh:23-27` enforces the protected-doc boundary with a raw `basename` match only. On the stock macOS/APFS case-insensitive path this was written for, `router.md` / `Router.md` can still resolve to `ROUTER.md`, and an alias symlink like `notes.md -> ROUTER.md` bypasses the check entirely and turns the sink back into a self-edit path. Fix: reject symlink targets (`[ -L "$TARGET" ]`), normalize the basename with `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'`, and compare that normalized name against the protected set before appending.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:62:- [Should] `test/phase3-signoff-guard.sh:10-16,39-50` does not carry the GH-44 safety fence that the DoD calls out for git-touching fixtures. It relies on `_setup.sh` scratch clones succeeding, but `_setup.sh` is not `set -e`; if the scratch repo setup degrades, `rtl_init` can still run without an explicit ceiling or `.git` assertion. Fix: export `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` to the scratch root before sourcing `relay-turn-lib.sh`, and assert `[ -d "$A/.git" ]` before each `rtl_init` call that depends on scratch-repo git state.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:79:Static review only; per relay rules I did not execute the artifact scripts.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:81:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/proposals-sink.sh:21-35,44-52` still has a same-inode bypass: an innocently named hard link such as `notes.md` hard-linked to `ROUTER.md` is neither a symlink nor a protected basename, so the append lands in the protected doc anyway and reopens the exact self-edit path this sink is supposed to close. `test/phase3-signoff-guard.sh:43-57` regression-tests symlinks and case variants but not this path. Fix: add a same-file check with `test -ef` against the protected docs (at minimum protected-name siblings in the target dir, and ideally the canonical repo docs too), and add a hard-link regression case to `phase3-signoff-guard.sh`.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:82:- [Should] `relay-automation/proposals-sink.sh:44-54` reports success even when the append itself fails. The grouped append uses `>> "$TARGET"` without checking its exit status; if the parent dir is missing or the file is unwritable, bash returns a redirection error, then the script still prints `appended N proposal(s)` and exits 0. That makes the sink lie about having preserved the Reviewer’s proposals. Fix: gate the append in an `if ! { ...; } >>"$TARGET"; then ...; exit 1; fi` block and only emit the success line after a verified write; add a negative test in `test/phase3-signoff-guard.sh` for an unwritable or nonexistent target path.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:99:Static review only; per relay rules I did not execute the artifact scripts.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:101:- [Blocker] `relay-automation/proposals-sink.sh:37-50` still leaves one trust-boundary bypass open. The same-inode guard only compares `$TARGET` against protected-name siblings in the target dir and `"$GROOT/$name"`, but `PROJECT/PDDA.md` is canonical at `"$repo_root/PROJECT/PDDA.md"`, not `"$repo_root/PDDA.md"`, and `GROOT` is derived from the target's git root rather than the sink repo's root. A hard link like `notes.md -> <this repo>/PROJECT/PDDA.md` from another directory/repo is neither a symlink nor a protected basename, so the append still lands in a protected rule doc. `test/phase3-signoff-guard.sh:59-74` regression-tests only `ROUTER.md`, so this hole is untested. Fix: derive the canonical root from the sink script path, compare against an explicit protected-path list that includes `PROJECT/PDDA.md`, and add a hard-link regression for that nested doc from a non-sibling target dir.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:102:- [Should] `relay-automation/proposals-sink.sh:45` is not path-with-spaces safe. `${GROOT:+"$GROOT/$name"}` is expanded unquoted in the `for` list, so a repo root like `/tmp/repo with spaces` word-splits and the `test -ef` check stops examining the real canonical path. That violates the shell-hygiene DoD for spaced paths and can silently weaken the hard-link guard. Fix: avoid unquoted list expansion here; check each candidate in separately quoted branches or build a quoted candidate array first.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-29/gh40-codeqa.md:113:**Operator disposition — closing the relay.** Across 3 rounds Codex confirmed each prior fix as [Pass] and surfaced progressively more contrived vectors on the same 50-line file (case/symlink → hard-link/append → nested-doc-hard-link/spaces; next would be a TOCTOU between the `-ef` check and the append — out of this caller's threat model). The substantive review **converged**: every real correctness/safety issue is fixed and re-confirmed. The trust boundary now refuses protected basenames (case-insensitive), symlinks, hard links (sibling + canonical incl. nested), and unwritable targets, and is space-safe. Per the operator's call, capping here rather than chasing diminishing returns. Thanks Codex — genuinely valuable review (the original case/symlink Blocker was real).

When a choice is unclear, the option that keeps agents synchronized, contained, and verifiable — without leaking or destroying work — wins. AGENTS.md is the behavioral playbook; ROUTER.md is the entry-point map; this is the *why*.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:158:     7	`tick` coordinates Claude Code, Codex, and agy (Antigravity CLI) on the same branch without collision: a shared local event log under `.tick/events/`, claims serialized by `O_EXCL` locks, and a `Marathon` harness that chains multi-phase build→review cycles from a `MARATHON.yaml`. The relay layer (`relay-automation/`) drives headless turns, isolates agent writes to worktrees, and enforces an allowlist so no headless agent destroys work it didn't intend to touch. The goal: a multi-agent swarm safe enough to run against a real external codebase and correct enough that its output is worth shipping.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:164:    13	- **Attested** — carries its receipts: source, evidence, confidence. /Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:169:    18	Fail a pillar, and the turn, feature, or relay review isn't done.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:173:    22	1. **Coordination is local-transport only.** `.tick/events/` is the shared bus; claims resolve from there, not from a remote. No per-event push/fetch; no remote dependency at runtime. A coordination primitive that reaches out is a coordination primitive that can fail or leak.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:175:    24	2. **One canonical event log; every surface is a projection.** `tick` accretes events; `STATE.md` is the current projection. Reads go through the projection; writes go through a `claim/take/scope/done` verb. Nothing canonical lives in two places where it can drift. An agent that hard-codes state outside `.tick/` is creating drift.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:177:    26	3. **Containment is non-negotiable.** A headless turn must not: self-commit mid-turn, orphan a peer's concurrent commit, or write outside its allowlist. The allowlist, worktree isolation, and commit-bypass guard exist because a driven agent will do all three if unconstrained — not hypothetically, but as documented live incidents (GH-13, GH-14, GH-17). New relay paths must clear the containment bar before they ship.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/refresh-v1-qa-213244/refresh-v1-qa.codex.md:179:    28	4. **Skill-first; never improvise the harness.** The `relay-xyz` skill owns the locator, sandbox rules, exit codes, and the safety boundary. The `PreToolUse` guard (`relay-automation/hooks/relay-xyz-guard.sh`) enforces this by blocking driver calls before the skill loads. Add capabilities to the skill; do not work around it.

When a choice is unclear, the option that keeps agents synchronized, contained, and verifiable — without leaking or destroying work — wins. AGENTS.md is the behavioral playbook; ROUTER.md is the entry-point map; this is the *why*.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/p51-design-080020/p51-design.codex.md:373:     7	`tick` coordinates Claude Code, Codex, and agy (Antigravity CLI) on the same branch without collision: a shared local event log under `.tick/events/`, claims serialized by `O_EXCL` locks, and a `Marathon` harness that chains multi-phase build→review cycles from a `MARATHON.yaml`. The relay layer (`relay-automation/`) drives headless turns, isolates agent writes to worktrees, and enforces an allowlist so no headless agent destroys work it didn't intend to touch. The goal: a multi-agent swarm safe enough to run against a real external codebase and correct enough that its output is worth shipping.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/p51-design-080020/p51-design.codex.md:379:    13	- **Attested** — carries its receipts: source, evidence, confidence. /Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/p51-design-080020/p51-design.codex.md:384:    18	Fail a pillar, and the turn, feature, or relay review isn't done.
/Users/noelsaw/Documents/GH Repos/xyz-3-agents-swarm/relay-system/2026-06-27/p51-design-080020/p51-design.codex.md:388:    22	1. **Coordination is local-transport only.** `.tick/events/` is the shared bus; claims resolve from there, not from a remote. No per-event push/fetch; no remote dependency at runtime. A coordination primitive that reaches out is a coordination primitive that can fail or leak.

   281	/**
   282	 * Reads the event log, projects it, and writes both `.tick/STATE.md` (the
   283	 * human-readable state) and `.tick/rejected.jsonl` (the fenced-event audit
   284	 * log, fully rewritten each call so it's always a deterministic mirror of the
   285	 * current event set).
   286	 * @param {string} repoRoot - absolute path to the repo root
   287	 * @returns {{tasks: Map<string, Object>, stateFile: string, rejections: Object[], rejectedFile: string}}
   288	 */
   289	function project(repoRoot) {
   290	  const events = readAllEvents(repoRoot);
   291	  const { tasks, rejections } = foldWithMeta(events);
   292	  const body = renderState(tasks);
   293	  const stateFile = path.join(repoRoot, '.tick', 'STATE.md');
   294	  fs.writeFileSync(stateFile, body);
   295	
   296	  // Fenced-event audit log (R1 / R4). Rewritten in full each projection so it is
   297	  // a deterministic mirror of the current event set — one JSON object per line,
   298	  // ready for SIEM ingestion. Always truncate-write (empty when nothing fenced)
   299	  // so a stale log never lingers.
   300	  const rejectedFile = path.join(repoRoot, '.tick', 'rejected.jsonl');
   301	  fs.writeFileSync(rejectedFile, rejections.map(r => JSON.stringify(r)).join('\n') + (rejections.length ? '\n' : ''));
   302	
   303	  return { tasks, stateFile, rejections, rejectedFile };
   304	}

    97	/**
    98	 * Validates a parsed marathon plan and resolves `depends_on` into a
    99	 * deterministic topological execution order (authoring order preserved among
   100	 * equally-ready phases).
   101	 * @param {{phases: Object[]}} plan - as returned by {@link parseMarathonYaml}
   102	 * @returns {Object[]} phases in execution order
   103	 * @throws {Error} on an empty plan, duplicate id, missing required field, bad
   104	 *   `reviewer`, or an unknown/self/cyclic `depends_on`
   105	 */
   106	function resolveOrder(plan) {
   107	  const phases = plan.phases || [];
   108	  if (phases.length === 0) throw new Error('no phases defined');
   109	  const byId = new Map();
   110	  for (const p of phases) {
   111	    if (!p.id) throw new Error('a phase is missing its id');
   112	    if (byId.has(p.id)) throw new Error(`duplicate phase id: ${p.id}`);
   113	    if (!p.reviewer) throw new Error(`phase ${p.id}: missing reviewer`);
   114	    if (!/^(codex|gemini)/.test(p.reviewer)) {
   115	      throw new Error(`phase ${p.id}: reviewer '${p.reviewer}' must start with codex or gemini`);
   116	    }
   117	    if (p.depends_on === p.id) throw new Error(`phase ${p.id}: depends_on itself`);
   118	    byId.set(p.id, p);
   119	  }
   120	  for (const p of phases) {
   121	    if (p.depends_on && !byId.has(p.depends_on)) {
   122	      throw new Error(`phase ${p.id}: depends_on unknown phase '${p.depends_on}'`);
   123	    }
   124	  }
   125	  // Topological sort (single-parent depends_on chain, but handle a general DAG deterministically:
   126	  // preserve authoring order among ready nodes).
   127	  const order = [];
   128	  const done = new Set();
   129	  const remaining = phases.slice();
   130	  let guard = 0;
   131	  while (remaining.length) {
   132	    if (guard++ > phases.length + 1) throw new Error('dependency cycle detected');
   133	    let progressed = false;
   134	    for (let i = 0; i < remaining.length; i++) {
   135	      const p = remaining[i];
   136	      if (!p.depends_on || done.has(p.depends_on)) {
   137	        order.push(p);
   138	        done.add(p.id);
   139	        remaining.splice(i, 1);
   140	        progressed = true;
   141	        break; // restart scan to keep authoring order deterministic
   142	      }
   143	    }
   144	    if (!progressed) throw new Error('dependency cycle detected');
   145	  }
   146	  return order;
   147	}
   148	
   149	module.exports = { parseMarathonYaml, resolveOrder };

     4	build swarms. Built in phases on top of `tick` (see
     5	[PROPOSAL-AUTOMATION.md](../PROJECT/1-INBOX/EXP-AUTOMATION/PROPOSAL-AUTOMATION.md)).
     6	
     7	**Execution contract: default live-window flow** — the default operator path is
     8	still the poll-driven, live-window flow: a Claude window under `/loop`, or a
     9	human one-line nudge when the turn belongs to a non-Claude window. Headless
    10	turn-takers now exist for Codex and agy (`codex-turn.sh`, `agy-turn.sh`).
    11	`relay-loop.sh --background --cross-model-cmd <shim>` can now auto-fire one of
    12	those shims on `DECISION: nudge-cross-model`; without that wrapper-only flag,
    13	the loop still degrades to the existing manual nudge. For the current headless path, see
    14	[the headless bring-up below](#headless-bring-up-codex--agy), plus
    15	[CROSSMODEL-OPTIONA-PLAN.md](CROSSMODEL-OPTIONA-PLAN.md).
    16	
    17	## Components
    18	| Script | Role |
    19	|---|---|
    20	| `poll.sh` | **Phase 4** per-tick poll driver. Reads state, applies the guard, dispatches `runner.sh`/`watchdog.sh` or idles. Run under `/loop`. |
    21	| `relay-loop.sh` | **GH-33 Phase 2/3 + GH-46 Phase 4** adaptive-cadence wrapper over `poll.sh` (which stays a pure oracle). Default = one tick that prints `NEXT-POLL: <s>` for a `/loop` dynamic tick / cron / any scheduler; `--sleep-loop` self-paces in pure bash (no Claude dep). **`--background`** dispatches the turn DETACHED on `run-runner`, and on `nudge-cross-model` it dispatches `--cross-model-cmd` only when that command is configured and reachable; otherwise it prints the same manual nudge `poll.sh` would have emitted. A pidfile (`<relay-file>.bgpid` or `--bg-pidfile`) is still the single-turn lock (`BG-RUNNING`, no double-dispatch; stale pidfile cleared before the fresh decision acts). Containment is **inherited** — the backgrounded process is the same runner/shim boundary, so the `relay-turn-lib.sh` boundary is byte-identical (`&` changes only when the parent returns). |
    22	| `runner.sh` | **Phase 3** single agent/turn: claim → run (`--agent-cmd`) → verdict gate (`VERDICT: PASS\|FAIL\|PARKED`) → done/retry; artifact-scoped clean-tree gate. |
    23	| `watchdog.sh` | **Phase 2** liveness: `tick analyze --format json` → parked `parked_suspects[]` → structured escalation record; reap gated behind `--allow-reap` (stub, pending an authority decision). |
    24	| `relay-drive.sh` | **Phase 4b** relay supervisor: loops a `/relay` Producer↔Reviewer thread to termination via a turn-taker; round cap + no-progress escalation. |
    25	| `relay-turn-lib.sh` | **Shared safety core** (sourced, not run): the model-agnostic containment contract — path-allowlist + commit-bypass guard + no-push. Both headless turn-takers source this so the boundary lives in ONE place. See [decisions/2026-06-15-unattended-agent-containment.md](../decisions/2026-06-15-unattended-agent-containment.md). |
    26	| `codex-turn.sh` | **Option-A** headless turn-taker for the **Codex** agent (`codex exec`); thin dispatch wrapper over `relay-turn-lib.sh`. |
    27	| `gemini-turn.sh` | **DEPRECATED 2026-06-19** — Gemini CLI retired; use `agy-turn.sh` instead. Kept as historical reference. |
    28	| `agy-turn.sh` | **Option-A** headless turn-taker for the **agy** (Antigravity CLI) agent (`agy -p`); thin dispatch wrapper over `relay-turn-lib.sh`. Permanent replacement for `gemini-turn.sh`; live-validated 2026-06-18. |
    29	| `aider-turn.sh` | Headless turn-taker for **Aider ↔ OpenRouter** (`aider --model openrouter/… --message`) — an OpenAI-standard lane discrete from Codex. Same `relay-turn-lib.sh` containment; because Aider is a file-editor (no mid-turn shell), the SHIM performs the tick token ops itself and runs Aider with `--no-auto-commits` (the harness owns the commit). Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` + `AIDER_MODEL` (e.g. `openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`, `openrouter/openai/gpt-4o`, `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat`). Works in **both** a marathon `--builder aider` lane AND a plain `/relay` — it routes through the shared `marathon-agent.sh` dispatcher (`relay-drive.sh`'s `--agent-cmd`), so a driven relay with `RELAY_AGENT=aider` fires it just like Codex/agy. |
    30	| `consult.sh` | Parallel read-only consult: asks the same question to **Codex, agy, and (opt-in) Aider↔OpenRouter** (`--models codex,agy,aider`), captures each transcript, and leaves synthesis to the caller. Advisory-only; also the engine behind `relay-drive.sh --consult-verify`. |

The worked form of the hands-free Path B in the `relay-xyz` skill. |

    40	## Operator usage (default live-window flow)
    41	
    42	### Hands-free relay turn (all-Claude only)
    43	In each Claude window, run a guarded `/loop` that uses `poll.sh` as the gate, then
    44	takes the turn from the relay file's embedded `▶ TAKE YOUR TURN` instructions:
    45	```
    46	# Producer window (agent id = the agent the RELAY-TURN token is handed to)
    47	/loop 60s run relay-automation/poll.sh --mode relay --agent claude-a \
    48	  --relay-file relay-system/<date>/<slug>.md --artifact <path-under-review> --dry-run ;\
    49	  if it prints "DECISION: run-runner", take your turn on that relay file per its embedded \
    50	  instructions (review/produce, append your block, `tick release RELAY-TURN --to <other>` or
    51	  `done` on approve, commit, push); otherwise do nothing.
    52	# Reviewer window: same, with that window's --agent id
    53	```
    54	**Whose-turn is the `RELAY-TURN` tick task** (handed off via `tick release --to`), so the
    55	Phase-1 handoff-exclusive rule + the Phase-2 watchdog both apply. The guard *is* the lock:
    56	a window acts only when the token is claimable by **its** agent **and** the artifact scope is
    57	clean. `poll.sh` exits `10` on a closed relay (file `STATUS: Approved|Closed`) so the loop can stop.
    58	*(Default `--relay-task RELAY-TURN`; seed it at relay setup, handed to the first actor.)*
    59	
    60	**Poll interval — cache-warmth tradeoff.** `60s` keeps Claude Code's prompt cache warm
    61	(≈5-min TTL); the **lock/heartbeat is the real correctness guard, not the timer**, so a longer
    62	interval only adds latency, never a race. Use ~`60s` for active relays, longer (e.g. `120s`)
    63	for the lower-frequency watchdog poller.
    64	
    65	**Self-closing loops (no stray cron housekeeping).** Launch each loop with a deadline so it
    66	ends on the first of: relay `Approved`/`Closed`, **or** the deadline:
    67	`--deadline "$(date -v+30M +%s)"` (macOS) / `--deadline "$(date -d '+30 min' +%s)"` (GNU).
    68	Past the deadline `poll.sh` prints `DECISION: stop`; the loop prompt then `CronList`s and
    69	`CronDelete`s its own job. Cron jobs are per-session — you can't stop another window's loop
    70	from yours, so always set a deadline. See the `/relay` skill → "Self-closing loops".
    71	
    72	### Designated watchdog (exactly ONE window)
    73	Only one poller holds watchdog authority, so a stalled turn is escalated once
    74	without double-escalation:
    75	```
    76	/loop 120s run relay-automation/poll.sh --mode relay --agent coordinator \
    77	  --relay-file relay-system/<date>/<slug>.md --watchdog-authority ;\
    78	  if it prints "DECISION: run-watchdog", it has escalated the parked turn — surface it to me.
    79	```
    80	
    81	### Single-process relay supervision (one window drives the whole thread)
    82	```
    83	relay-automation/relay-drive.sh --relay-file relay-system/<date>/<slug>.md \
    84	  --agent-cmd "<turn-taker>" --round-cap 6
    85	```
    86	`--agent-cmd` is the turn-taker seam. In the live-window flow it can remain a
    87	window-driven/manual handoff; in the current headless path it can be a shipped
    88	shim such as `relay-automation/codex-turn.sh` or `relay-automation/agy-turn.sh`.
    89	Exits: `0` closed Approved/Closed, `3` no-progress, `4` round cap / closed-not-approved, `5`
    90	(with `--review-once`) reviewer completed a single non-approval review. Inspect whose-turn mid-drive
    91	with `tick info <task>` (the verb is `info`, not `status`).
    92	
    93	### Cross-model windows (Codex / agy)
    94	In the poll-based multi-window flow, non-Claude windows still need a wake-up path.
    95	Without `relay-loop.sh --background --cross-model-cmd <shim>`, the operator's
    96	whole job is **one line**:
    97	```
    98	take your turn on relay-system/<date>/<slug>.md
    99	```
   100	The relay file embeds the `▶ TAKE YOUR TURN` instructions, so any agent acts from
   101	the file alone. `poll.sh` detects a cross-model turn and emits this nudge text
   102	rather than silently idling. If you want the current headless cross-model path
   103	inside the `/loop` poll flow, wrap `poll.sh` with `relay-loop.sh --background`
   104	and pass `--cross-model-cmd relay-automation/codex-turn.sh` (or `agy-turn.sh`);
   105	the same pidfile lock prevents a second dispatch while that shim is still
   106	running. `relay-drive.sh` remains the deterministic single-window alternative.
   107	
   108	## Boundary (load-bearing)
   109	- **Hands-free poll is all-Claude only** — it relies on Claude Code's in-session `/loop`. Cross-model stays on the manual nudge.
   110	- **Not a durable scheduler / not unattended-without-a-window.** A Claude window must be open and looping for the default poll flow. Current headless turns exist, but durable unattended orchestration is still a separate problem.
   111	- The portable `/relay` skill stays dependency-free; this tick-driven automation lives here.
   112	
   113	## Headless bring-up (Codex + agy)
   114	
   115	This section is the canonical fresh-device bootstrap path for the two shipped
   116	headless Path-A workers: Codex and agy.
   117	
   118	> **What a single-device test proves.** `.tick/` is gitignored and device-local,
   119	> so two clones do not share token state over git. A fresh-device run proves
   120	> that the selected headless turn-taker works cleanly in a fresh clone behind
   121	> the safety shim; it does not prove cross-machine coordination.
   122	
   123	### 1. Prerequisites
   124	
   125	The shipped scripts assume Node, git, and whichever headless worker you plan to
   126	drive:
   127	
   128	```bash
   129	node --version
   130	codex exec -s workspace-write "create a file ok.txt with the text ok" < /dev/null   # Codex lane
   131	agy -p "Reply with exactly: PONG" < /dev/null                                        # agy lane; run sandbox-OFF
   132	git --version
   133	```
   134	
   135	Run the worker check for the lane you actually plan to drive; run both if you
   136	want both workers available on that machine.
   137	
   138	The Codex autonomy check matters: a bare `codex exec "say ok"` can succeed without
   139	proving Codex can write the relay file. `codex-turn.sh` defaults to
   140	`-s workspace-write`; if your device config still blocks writes, set
   141	`CODEX_FLAGS='--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox'` or add
   142	`-c approval_policy=never`. If `codex` is not on `PATH` or is not authenticated,
   143	fix that before running the shim; override the binary with
   144	`CODEX_BIN=/path/to/codex` if needed.
   145	
   146	The agy check must also run unsandboxed. `agy-turn.sh` uses `agy -p`; when agy's
   147	backend is blocked by a sandbox it can exit `0` with empty output, which the
   148	shim correctly treats as a failed turn. If `agy` is not on `PATH` or is not
   149	authenticated through the Antigravity desktop app, fix that before driving the
   150	lane; override the binary with `AGY_BIN=/path/to/agy` if needed. Antigravity
   151	installs `agy` at `~/.local/bin/agy` on macOS by default (not on the system
   152	PATH); running `AGY_BIN=~/.local/bin/agy bash test/agy-turn.sh` confirms it
   153	works before adding it to your PATH or passing `AGY_BIN` to every drive command.
   154	
   155	If you are running under a sandboxed AI shell, run both workers outside that
   156	sandbox. Codex often fails there because it cannot reach the OS keychain or
   157	`chatgpt.com`; agy can fail "cleanly" with empty output when its backend network
   158	is blocked.
   159	
   160	### 2. Clone or refresh the harness
   161	
   162	```bash
   163	git clone https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm.git
   164	cd xyz-3-agents-swarm
   165	# or, in an existing clone: git pull origin main
   166	export TICK_REPO_ROOT="$PWD"
   167	```
   168	
   169	### 3. Smoke test the local machine
   170	
   171	Run the repo gate, then the shim test for the worker you plan to drive:
   172	
   173	```bash
   174	bash validate.sh
   175	bash test/codex-turn.sh   # before Codex runs
   176	bash test/agy-turn.sh     # before agy runs
   177	```
   178	
   179	If `validate.sh` cannot make tempdirs, that is usually a sandbox blocking
   180	`mktemp`; rerun it in a normal shell.
   181	
   182	### 4. Drive one headless turn in this repo
   183	
   184	The supervisor (`relay-drive.sh`) drives the turn; the selected shim
   185	(`codex-turn.sh` or `agy-turn.sh`) is the turn-taker and owns the safety
   186	boundary: path allowlist, commit-bypass guard, file-scoped commit, and no push.
   187	*(Note: Fixed log paths break concurrent same-machine runs. Prefer using the shims' default per-PID paths or specifying a per-PID log file path with `$$`.)*
   188	
   189	**Worktree isolation is ON by default for driven runs.** `relay-drive.sh`
   190	exports `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=1`, so each shim runs inside a throwaway
   191	`git worktree` of `ROOT@HEAD`. Off-allowlist writes in the worktree are
   192	discarded and the turn fails with **exit 6**. One important side-effect: agents
   193	that write to the relay file via **absolute paths** bypass the worktree (those
   194	writes land in ROOT, not the throwaway tree) — so untracked relay files with
   195	absolute paths in the `▶ TAKE YOUR TURN` block remain accessible to the agent.
   196	Opt out per run with `RELAY_WORKTREE_ISOLATION=0` if you need to disable
   197	isolation (e.g. during testing).
   198	
   199	#### Codex worker
   200	
   201	```bash
   202	# Reuse an existing relay thread or scaffold a fresh one with embedded
   203	# TAKE YOUR TURN instructions.
   204	RELAY=relay-system/$(date +%F)/<your-slug>.md
   205	ARTIFACT=relay-automation/codex-turn.sh
   206	
   207	# Use a per-relay token id, not the literal RELAY-TURN.
   208	TASK="RELAY-$(basename "$RELAY" .md)"
   209	
   210	./bin/tick log task.created "$TASK" --agent claude-a
   211	./bin/tick claim   "$TASK" --agent claude-a --paths "$ARTIFACT"
   212	./bin/tick release "$TASK" --agent claude-a --to codex
   213	
   214	CODEX_AGENT=codex ALLOW_PATHS="$ARTIFACT" CODEX_LOG="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codex-turn-$$.log" \
   215	relay-automation/relay-drive.sh \
   216	  --relay-file "$RELAY" \
   217	  --relay-task "$TASK" \
   218	  --agent-cmd relay-automation/codex-turn.sh \
   219	  --round-cap 4
   220	```
   221	
   222	Expect Codex to claim and ping the token, append its block to the relay file,
   223	release or `done` the token, revert any off-allowlist edits, commit only the
   224	allowlisted paths, and skip push. The transcript lands in
   225	`"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codex-turn-$$.log"`.
   226	
   227	#### agy worker
   228	
   229	```bash
   230	# Reuse an existing relay thread or scaffold a fresh one with embedded
   231	# TAKE YOUR TURN instructions.
   232	RELAY=relay-system/$(date +%F)/<your-slug>.md
   233	ARTIFACT=relay-automation/agy-turn.sh
   234	
   235	# Use a per-relay token id, not the literal RELAY-TURN.
   236	TASK="RELAY-$(basename "$RELAY" .md)"
   237	
   238	./bin/tick log task.created "$TASK" --agent claude-a
   239	./bin/tick claim   "$TASK" --agent claude-a --paths "$ARTIFACT"
   240	./bin/tick release "$TASK" --agent claude-a --to agy

===== guard =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# relay-xyz-guard.sh — PreToolUse guard that stops a session from driving the relay
     4	# harness before it has actually loaded the relay-xyz skill.
     5	#
     6	# The recurring failure this closes: a session runs `ls relay-automation/`, assumes it
     7	# understands the handoff, and improvises its own harness instead of invoking the
     8	# relay-xyz skill. The skill's content can't fix that, because the agent never opens it.
     9	# A hook can — the harness executes it, not the model, so a confident agent can't skip it.
    10	#
    11	# Wiring (.claude/settings.json):
    12	#   "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash|Skill",
    13	#     "hooks": [ { "type": "command",
    14	#       "command": "bash relay-automation/hooks/relay-xyz-guard.sh" } ] } ] }
    15	#
    16	# Contract (reads the PreToolUse JSON event on stdin):
    17	#   - PROOF-OF-LOAD signals → record this session as "skill loaded", then allow:
    18	#       * Skill tool invoked with skill == relay-xyz
    19	#       * Bash command that runs the skill's own locator (find-harness.sh)
    20	#   - BLOCK (exit 2, message to the model) when a Bash command EXECUTES a harness driver
    21	#       entrypoint under relay-automation/ AND this session has not loaded the skill.
    22	#       Exit 2 feeds stderr back to the model and cancels the tool call.
    23	#   - Everything else → exit 0 (allow). Fail-open: any parse error allows the call.
    24	#
    25	# Precision notes:
    26	#   - Only relay-automation/<driver>.sh paths block — test/<driver>.sh and reads are exempt,
    27	#     so `validate.sh` and the shim tests never trip it.
    28	#   - Session-scoped via the event's session_id, so a marker from one session never
    29	#     suppresses the guard in another.
    30	set -u
    31	
    32	input="$(cat)"
    33	
    34	# Extract (session_id, tool_name, field) with python3 — robust JSON, no jq dependency.
    35	# field = the Skill name for Skill events, else the Bash command. Tabs/newlines stripped
    36	# from field so the tab-delimited read below stays single-line; session_id is read first
    37	# and tool second so the variable-length field can safely land last.
    38	parsed="$(RELAY_GUARD_EVENT="$input" python3 <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
    39	import os, json
    40	try:
    41	    d = json.loads(os.environ.get("RELAY_GUARD_EVENT", ""))
    42	except Exception:
    43	    raise SystemExit(0)
    44	tool = d.get("tool_name", "") or ""
    45	ti = d.get("tool_input", {}) or {}
    46	if tool == "Skill":
    47	    field = ti.get("skill", "") or ti.get("name", "")
    48	else:
    49	    field = ti.get("command", "")
    50	sess = d.get("session_id", "") or "nosession"
    51	field = str(field).replace("\t", " ").replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", " ")
    52	print("%s\t%s\t%s" % (sess, tool, field))
    53	PY
    54	)"
    55	
    56	# Parse error or empty → fail open.
    57	[ -n "$parsed" ] || exit 0
    58	IFS=$'\t' read -r SESSION TOOL FIELD <<EOF
    59	$parsed
    60	EOF
    61	
    62	STATE_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/relay-xyz-guard"
    63	mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
    64	MARKER="$STATE_DIR/${SESSION//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
    65	
    66	# --- proof-of-load: the skill was actually invoked this session ---
    67	if [ "$TOOL" = "Skill" ]; then
    68	  case "$FIELD" in *relay-xyz*) : > "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac
    69	  exit 0
    70	fi
    71	
    72	[ "$TOOL" = "Bash" ] || exit 0
    73	
    74	# Running the skill's own locator is the Preconditions step the skill mandates —
    75	# treat it as proof the skill is being followed.
    76	case "$FIELD" in
    77	  *find-harness.sh*) : > "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0 ;;
    78	esac
    79	
    80	# Inspection (read-only) of a harness file is not "driving" — never block it.
    81	first="${FIELD%% *}"
    82	case "$first" in
    83	  cat|head|tail|less|more|wc|grep|rg|ls|bat|file|stat|chmod|git|find|awk|sed) exit 0 ;;
    84	esac
    85	case "$FIELD" in *"bash -n "*) exit 0 ;; esac
    86	
    87	# --- driver entrypoints: executing these IS driving the harness ---
    88	case "$FIELD" in
    89	  *relay-automation/relay-drive.sh*|\
    90	  *relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh*|\
    91	  *relay-automation/marathon.sh*|\
    92	  *relay-automation/poll.sh*|\
    93	  *relay-automation/codex-turn.sh*|\
    94	  *relay-automation/agy-turn.sh*)
    95	    if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
    96	      cat >&2 <<'MSG'
    97	relay-xyz guard — STOP. You are about to drive the relay harness, but the relay-xyz
    98	skill has not been loaded in this session.
    99	
   100	Invoke the relay-xyz skill FIRST (Skill tool → relay-xyz). Do not hand-roll the handoff
   101	or build your own harness from `ls relay-automation/`. The skill owns:
   102	  • the device-agnostic locator (find-harness.sh) — never hardcode a path
   103	  • the Bash-sandbox rules for the codex/agy subprocess
   104	  • the exit codes and the containment / safety boundary (path-allowlist, no push)
   105	
   106	If you have already read it, run the skill's Preconditions block (find-harness.sh) and retry.
   107	MSG
   108	      exit 2
   109	    fi
   110	    ;;
   111	esac
   112	
   113	exit 0

   153	## Discovery & spike phases
   154	
   155	Discovery and spike phases exist to *learn* — reverse-engineer an existing system, probe an unknown,
   156	prove or kill a risky approach before committing the plan to it. Their output is knowledge, and under
   157	Principle #1 (*docs are the runtime state, not a record of it*) that knowledge is project state. If it
   158	lives only in an agent's context or a throwaway scratch note, a cold agent resuming the plan cannot see
   159	what was learned, why a path was chosen or abandoned, or what the spike actually proved — and the work
   160	gets re-done.
   161	
   162	Contract: **a phase tagged as discovery or spike must write its findings back into the originating plan
   163	doc before its QA gate can pass.** Concretely, that phase's section (or a clearly linked sibling
   164	section in the same doc) must capture:
   165	
   166	- **what was investigated** — the system/area reverse-engineered or the question the spike asked
   167	- **what was found** — the concrete mechanics learned, with repo-relative pointers (`file:line`) where
   168	  the finding lives in code, not a vague summary
   169	- **what it changes** — how the finding confirms, redirects, or kills the plan's later phases; an
   170	  unfinished "we'll know after the spike" left dangling is itself the gap
   171	
   172	This satisfies Principle #4 (*one canonical place per fact*): the originating plan is that place. A
   173	spike whose findings sit in chat is the exact drift PDDA exists to prevent. The QA gate for a
   174	discovery/spike phase therefore includes "findings are written back to this doc" as an acceptance
   175	criterion alongside the phase's normal checks.
   176	
   177	Enforcement is **advisory (LLM layer, warn-capped)** — `pdda-doc-ready.sh` flags a discovery/spike
   178	phase whose findings were not written back. "Did the agent actually capture what it learned" is a
   179	judgment a regex cannot make honestly, so it stays with the LLM reviewer and, like every finding from
   180	that layer, never blocks a build (see [LLM-assisted doc readiness review](#2-llm-assisted-doc-readiness-review)).

===== hooks section =====
   437	### 3. Doc-health hooks (event-triggered delivery)
   438	
   439	The deterministic checks above can also run automatically from Claude Code hooks, as a two-tier
   440	doc-health system. The hooks are pure **delivery** — they run the SAME section-1 checks on a trigger;
   441	they add no new analysis class. Both are **warn-only and fail-open: they always exit `0` and can never
   442	block** an edit or a stop (a doc-hygiene reminder is never worth interrupting work — the calibration
   443	principle, same as `pdda.sh changelog`).
   444	
   445	- **Tier 1 — `pdda-edit-doc-hook.sh` (`PostToolUse` on `Edit|Write|MultiEdit`).** Reads the edited
   446	  `tool_input.file_path`; exits `0` instantly unless it is `ROADMAP.md` or a `PROJECT/**/*.md` doc;
   447	  otherwise runs the fast **local single-file** subset for just that file — `frontmatter`,
   448	  `status-table`, `hardcoded-paths`, `roadmap-coverage` (and `roadmap` for `ROADMAP.md`), scoped via
   449	  `PDDA_ONLY_FILE`. **No network, no `gh`, no LLM**, so it stays instant and cannot gate an edit.
   450	- **Tier 2 — Stop full-scan (`pdda-stop-doc-health.sh`).** The companion that runs one consolidated,
   451	  system-wide doc-health scan per turn (the deterministic suite plus `issue-doc-sync` against the
   452	  cached gh-state file). See [Suggested Stop doc-health scan](#suggested-stop-doc-health-scan).
   453	
   454	`PDDA_ONLY_FILE=<path>` is the seam that scopes any check to a single file (unset = full scan, the
   455	default everywhere else). Wiring is repo-local in `.claude/settings.json`; installs receive the hook
   456	scripts via the manifest and opt in by adding the hook entries.
   457	
   458	#### Suggested Stop doc-health scan
   459	
   460	Tier 2's `pdda-stop-doc-health.sh` runs **one** system-wide scan per turn and prints a **single
   461	consolidated report**:
   462	
   463	- it runs the deterministic suite with `PDDA_ISSUE_SYNC_SOURCE=cache`, so `issue-doc-sync` reads the
   464	  cached gh-state file (written by `pdda.sh gh-refresh`) and the scan makes **no network call**;
   465	- it runs in `observe` mode with the LLM layer disabled — purely deterministic, fast, offline;
   466	- it aggregates the run into one report: a header with the error/warn totals, then the warn/error
   467	  finding lines (an `all clear` line when there are none);
   468	- it **always exits `0`** (proven by `test/pdda-doc-health-hooks.sh`), so it can never block a stop.
   469	
   470	Wire it as a `Stop` hook in `.claude/settings.json` (no matcher). Because it reads the cache rather
   471	than calling `gh`, keep `pdda.sh gh-refresh` on the hourly cadence so the Stop report stays current.
   472	
   473	## Enforcement modes
   474	
   475	PDDA runs in one of three modes. The mode is resolved in this order: **the `PDDA_MODE` env var wins if

The previous behavior unconditionally disabled worktree isolation whenever `.gitmodules` existed, which penalised every plan in a submodule project even when the plan was nowhere near a submodule. **Answer**
Phase 0 inventory is doable and mostly comes out clean: Family A is a real, explicit GSD discipline built around a five-step loop plus durable `.planning/` artifacts and fresh-context subagents, while Rebalance’s closest native counterpart is PDDA’s doc lifecycle and per-phase QA, not an equivalent `STATE.md`/`CONTEXT.md` runtime. Family B is also real: GSD’s `skills/`/`commands/`/`agents/`/`hooks/`/`capabilities/` stack is an actual composition system, not a thin naming layer; the closest counterparts here are the global Claude skill catalogs plus XYZ’s relay/tick harness, while Rebalance-native lacks a true capability-registry layer.

**Findings**
- [Should] The prompt assumes a vendored `.xyz/` tree in this checkout, but I could only verify `.xyz-pin`, not `.xyz/`; local “vendored XYZ” claims are therefore UNVERIFIED unless sourced from the canonical `xyz-3-agents-swarm` repo instead [`./.xyz-pin:1-17`].
- [Pass] GSD’s `capabilities/` layer is substantive, not cosmetic: it composes registry views across skills, agents, hooks, config keys, and loop extension points, with trust and fail-closed rules for executable surfaces [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/capability-overlay-model.md:18-40`, `49-82`, `184-236`; `gsd-core/docs/explanation/capability-trust-model.md:16-39`, `150-166`, `241-254`].
- [Pass] Rebalance already has a strong phase-doc discipline, but it does not have a GSD-style compact project-memory pair like `STATE.md` + per-phase `CONTEXT.md`; its state is spread across `ROADMAP.md`, active `PROJECT/**` docs, and optional snapshots [`PROJECT/PDDA.md:30-41`, `153-175`; `ROADMAP.md:9-12`, `22-23`; `giant-brains.../snapshot/SKILL.md:14-25`, `54-60`].

**Family A inventory**
- GSD’s loop is explicit: `Discuss → (UI design) → Plan → Execute → Verify → Ship`, with each step justified as a separate failure-prevention layer [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md:11-15`, `23-59`].
- The loop persists through `.planning/`: `STATE.md` is the navigation layer, and per-phase artifacts include `CONTEXT.md`, `RESEARCH.md`, `PLAN.md`, `SUMMARY.md`, `VERIFICATION.md`, and `UAT.md` [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md:96-104`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/planning-artifacts.md:9-39`, `72-89`, `120-189`].
- `STATE.md` is a compact living memory file read at the start of every workflow and written after significant actions, with explicit lifecycle fields like `active_phase`, `next_action`, and progress counters [`gsd-core/docs/reference/state-md.md:9-15`, `24-51`, `56-76`, `92-100`].
- `CONTEXT.md` is a sealed per-phase decision artifact, not freeform notes: fixed blocks like `<domain>`, `<decisions>`, `<canonical_refs>`, `<code_context>`, `<specifics>`, and `<deferred>` guide downstream research and planning [`gsd-core/docs/reference/context-md.md:21-48`, `52-63`, `66-92`; `gsd-core/gsd-core/workflows/discuss-phase/templates/context.md:27-136`].
- Fresh-context subagents are the core anti-rot mechanism: the orchestrator stays thin while researcher/planner/checker/executor/verifier agents start with clean windows and read only the artifacts they need [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/context-engineering.md:26-42`, `57-66`, `109-110`; `gsd-core/docs/explanation/multi-agent-orchestration.md:21-27`, `30-55`, `166-178`].
- Execution is wave-based: plans declare dependencies and waves, Wave 1 runs in parallel, later waves wait, and executors write `SUMMARY.md` plus atomic commits [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/multi-agent-orchestration.md:88-136`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/plan-md.md:27-60`, `66-76`, `218-240`].
- “Done” is gated by verification, not just completion: the verifier checks `must_haves`, coverage, and phase-goal alignment and emits `VERIFICATION.md` with routable statuses [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md:51-59`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/planning-artifacts.md:182-189`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/plan-md.md:79-99`].

**Family B inventory**
- The composition stack is explicit: command layer → workflow/orchestrator → specialized agents → CLI tools layer → filesystem state in `.planning/` [`gsd-core/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:31-65`, `110-144`, `207-217`].
- Worked example, `execute-phase`: the command/skill entrypoint loads `workflows/execute-phase.md` and exposes the runtime-facing surface [`gsd-core/commands/gsd/execute-phase.md:1-16`, `35-65`; `gsd-core/skills/gsd-execute-phase/SKILL.md:1-16`, `35-65`]. **Family A inventory**
- GSD’s loop is explicit: `Discuss → (UI design) → Plan → Execute → Verify → Ship`, with each step justified as a separate failure-prevention layer [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md:11-15`, `23-59`].
- The loop persists through `.planning/`: `STATE.md` is the navigation layer, and per-phase artifacts include `CONTEXT.md`, `RESEARCH.md`, `PLAN.md`, `SUMMARY.md`, `VERIFICATION.md`, and `UAT.md` [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md:96-104`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/planning-artifacts.md:9-39`, `72-89`, `120-189`].
- `STATE.md` is a compact living memory file read at the start of every workflow and written after significant actions, with explicit lifecycle fields like `active_phase`, `next_action`, and progress counters [`gsd-core/docs/reference/state-md.md:9-15`, `24-51`, `56-76`, `92-100`].
- `CONTEXT.md` is a sealed per-phase decision artifact, not freeform notes: fixed blocks like `<domain>`, `<decisions>`, `<canonical_refs>`, `<code_context>`, `<specifics>`, and `<deferred>` guide downstream research and planning [`gsd-core/docs/reference/context-md.md:21-48`, `52-63`, `66-92`; `gsd-core/gsd-core/workflows/discuss-phase/templates/context.md:27-136`].
- Fresh-context subagents are the core anti-rot mechanism: the orchestrator stays thin while researcher/planner/checker/executor/verifier agents start with clean windows and read only the artifacts they need [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/context-engineering.md:26-42`, `57-66`, `109-110`; `gsd-core/docs/explanation/multi-agent-orchestration.md:21-27`, `30-55`, `166-178`].
- Execution is wave-based: plans declare dependencies and waves, Wave 1 runs in parallel, later waves wait, and executors write `SUMMARY.md` plus atomic commits [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/multi-agent-orchestration.md:88-136`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/plan-md.md:27-60`, `66-76`, `218-240`].
- “Done” is gated by verification, not just completion: the verifier checks `must_haves`, coverage, and phase-goal alignment and emits `VERIFICATION.md` with routable statuses [`gsd-core/docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md:51-59`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/planning-artifacts.md:182-189`; `gsd-core/docs/reference/plan-md.md:79-99`].
